title: Tech Note: 4D v11 SQL Assimilator
author: Charles “Charlie” Vass, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: 4D v11 SQL Assimilator component using native 4D SQL to read system tables of external databases
ODBC-based connections to MySQL, SQL Server 2000, MS Access; direct connection to 4D v11 SQL Server
Wizard UI for table/field selection, record preview, and cycle-based (chunked) batch import
Automatic table/data-type migration into a new or existing 4D v11 SQL structure

historical_commentary.text: This note documents 4D's ODBC/native-SQL-based database migration wizard for pulling table structures and data from third-party SQL databases (or pre-v11 4D databases) into a new 4D v11 SQL structure, notable at the time because it was the first Assimilator built entirely on 4D's then-new native SQL engine rather than relying on ODBC plug-ins for everything. The core migration need (bring external data into 4D) is timeless, but this specific component, its ODBC/DSN-centric workflow, and its system-table-parsing implementation for long-superseded database versions (SQL Server 2000, MySQL 5-era, Access) reflect 2009-era interoperability tooling; 4D's SQL engine, connection options, and even the concept of assimilation tooling have evolved substantially since, and current migration approaches would typically favor modern connectors, direct database drivers, or custom SQL/ODBC scripts built against current-generation databases rather than this specific decade-old component.
related_updates: 4D's native SQL engine and supported database connectivity (ODBC drivers, direct connections) have been substantially updated since 2009, making the specific driver/version assumptions in this note outdated
Modern 4D data-migration needs are more commonly addressed with current ODBC/SQL connectivity or ORDA-based remote datastore access rather than this specific legacy Assimilator component
